title: Acne Bootcamp — 12-Week Face Reality Acne Program
tagline: The full Face Reality program — consult, biweekly treatments, adaptive home care
description: The Acne Bootcamp is the 12-week Face Reality Acne Program itself — the structured, guided path led by Amber, a Face Reality Certified Acne Specialist in Punta Gorda. It pairs biweekly in-studio visits with a customized daily home-care regimen and ongoing coaching, and it's sold as one complete program because those parts work together. Here's the rhythm: your first visit is a consultation and skin analysis where Amber grades the breakouts, reviews triggers, teaches you to read ingredient lists, and hands off your initial home-care routine — usually including a cleanse, extractions, and LED that day. Then, every two weeks for the program, you return for a double cleanse, an enzyme treatment or acne peel, expert extractions of ready congestion, and high-frequency and/or LED. At each visit Amber checks progress and adjusts your home care in small, measured steps — strengthening it before your skin gets used to it, but not so fast it becomes dry or irritated. That progressive adjustment is the core of the method, which is why the every-two-weeks cadence matters and the program is time-boxed. A purge can happen in the first few weeks and is temporary. Face Reality's method is designed to show visible improvement in roughly six to eight weeks, with more clearing over three to six months, depending heavily on your acne type and how consistently you follow the home care. Individual outcomes vary; we don't promise a timeframe. A Back/Chest Acne Add-On extends it to bacne.
who_its_for: The Bootcamp suits someone who wants a plan and accountability and is willing to do the daily home care and keep biweekly appointments for about twelve weeks — people fighting a recurring pattern of breakouts, not occasional congestion. Sensitive and melanin-rich skin prone to post-breakout dark marks is well served by the mandelic-forward approach. It isn't the right fit for deep cystic or nodular acne, widespread inflammation, or actively scarring acne, which warrants a dermatologist first; the program can complement medical care when coordinated with your physician. Anyone on or recently on isotretinoin should confirm timing at consultation, since certain treatments are paused around it. Because the whole method is built on daily adherence, clients unable to commit to the routine won't get the intended benefit. title: Botox & Neurotoxins
tagline: Botox & Daxxify — softened lines, natural movement
description: Neurotoxins, also called wrinkle relaxers or neuromodulators, are precision injections of botulinum toxin type A that temporarily relax the small facial muscles behind dynamic expression lines: the frown lines between the brows, horizontal forehead lines, and the crow's feet at the outer eyes. In plain English, those creases form because repeated muscle movement folds the skin over and over. A neurotoxin is injected in tiny amounts into the specific muscle and temporarily quiets the nerve signal that tells it to contract, so the muscle relaxes and the skin above it creases less. One level deeper: botulinum toxin type A cleaves SNAP-25, a protein the nerve needs to release acetylcholine, the messenger that triggers contraction. That effect is partial, localized, and reversible, and it wears off as nerve terminals regenerate over months, which is exactly why maintenance is part of the treatment. At House of Rose, Diana, our injecting RN, offers two options under medical-director oversight. Botox is the long-established standard, typically lasting about three to four months. Daxxify is a newer, peptide-stabilized neuromodulator with a median duration of roughly six months in trials. The visit is quick, around 20 minutes, with little to no downtime. Results build over about two weeks. The aim here is softened movement dosed to your anatomy, not a frozen look. Individual outcomes vary, and not every client is a candidate.
who_its_for: This is for adults bothered by dynamic expression lines, the frown, forehead, and crow's-feet lines that show up when you move, who want a subtle softening while keeping natural expression. Some clients start earlier as maintenance, since reducing repetitive folding can support the appearance of smoother skin over time. It is not the right tool for volume loss, deep static folds visible at rest, skin laxity, or surface texture; those call for filler, PRF, or resurfacing instead. Neurotoxins are not offered during pregnancy or breastfeeding, and certain neuromuscular conditions rule them out. Final candidacy, area selection, and dosing are always confirmed by Diana, RN, at consultation.

Q: What is the difference between Botox and Daxxify?
A: Both are botulinum toxin type A and work the same way, by temporarily relaxing the muscles that cause expression lines. Botox is the long-established standard and typically lasts about three to four months. Daxxify is a newer, peptide-stabilized option with a median duration of about six months in trials, and improvement out to nine months for some clients. The peptide is a stabilization difference, not a different action. Diana helps you choose based on how often you would prefer to come in.

Q: How long does it last, and when will I see results?
A: Botox typically lasts about three to four months; Daxxify's median in trials was about six months, with some clients seeing improvement out to nine. Individual outcomes vary with dose, area, muscle strength, and metabolism.

Q: Is Daxxify FDA-approved?

title: Dermaplaning
tagline: The glass-skin finish
description: Dermaplaning is a manual exfoliation treatment in which Amber uses a sterile, single-use blade to gently sweep away the outermost layer of dead surface skin cells and the fine vellus hair, the peach fuzz, on the face. Held at roughly a forty-five-degree angle and worked in light, feathery strokes on dry skin, the blade removes two things in one pass: the loose dead cells sitting on the surface and the fine hair on top of them. The result is skin that looks instantly smoother, brighter, and camera-ready, with a surface that takes makeup evenly and lets skincare absorb more readily. Because it clears that dulling layer, it is a favorite week-of treatment before weddings, photos, and events. About the myth that shaving or dermaplaning makes hair grow back thicker or darker: it does not. Vellus hair grows back the same size, shape, and color it was before, because cutting a hair at the surface does not change the follicle, its diameter, its growth rate, or its pigment. It removes only the tapered tip, which can make regrowth feel momentarily blunt, never actually thicker. This is a superficial, esthetician-grade exfoliation that works at the very top of the epidermis. It is comfortable and essentially downtime-free, though skin may look slightly pink or feel briefly tight. The glow lasts around three to four weeks as natural turnover restores the surface, so most clients maintain it about once a month. It is a smoothing and prep treatment, not a corrective or collagen-building one.
who_its_for: Dermaplaning suits clients who want an instant, low-downtime smoothing and brightening, anyone prepping for an event or photos, people bothered by peach fuzz that makes foundation look patchy, and those with dry, flaky, or dull-textured skin who want their skincare or a follow-on facial to work harder. It is also comfortable for people who dislike the tingle of chemical exfoliation. It is generally not appropriate over active acne breakouts, an active rosacea or eczema flare, cold sores, sunburn, or broken or very reactive skin, and it is not a substitute for waxing when the goal is coarse-hair removal, which is Aundrea's or Brandy's lane. Final candidacy is confirmed by the provider at consultation and skin analysis, and individual outcomes vary.

Q: Will the hair grow back thicker or darker?
A: No. Dermaplaning removes fine vellus, peach-fuzz, hair at the surface, and it grows back the same size, shape, and color it was before. Cutting a hair does not change the follicle, its thickness, or its pigment. This is the same well-worn shaving myth, and it applies here too.

Q: Does dermaplaning hurt, and is there any downtime?
A: Most clients find it painless and even relaxing, describing a light feathering or scraping sensation with no numbing needed. Downtime is essentially none; skin may look slightly pink or feel a touch tight briefly. It is a classic quick-turnaround, lunchtime-style treatment.

Q: How long do results last, and how often should I get it?
A: The smooth, bright finish typically lasts about three to four weeks as your skin's natural turnover cycle restores the surface layer and the vellus hair. Because skin turns over roughly monthly, most clients maintain the look with a session about once every four weeks, which is why a Package of 4 is offered. Your provider individualizes the spacing.

Q: Can I do it if I have active acne or rosacea?
A: Generally not during active acne breakouts, since the blade can irritate active lesions and spread bacteria. With rosacea it is approached with caution and not during a flare. If your skin is calm and clear, the provider will confirm candidacy at consultation; if it is inflamed or reactive, they will steer you toward gentler options.

Q: How does dermaplaning compare to facial waxing?
A: They do different jobs. Dermaplaning removes fine peach-fuzz vellus hair and exfoliates dead skin, so its main purpose is smoothing and brightening. Facial waxing pulls coarser hair from the root, so it lasts longer but does not exfoliate. Choose dermaplaning for glow and makeup-readiness; choose waxing for durable removal of more defined facial hair. Facial waxing is Aundrea's or Brandy's lane, not Amber's.

Q: How should I care for my skin afterward?
A: Wear broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher daily and limit direct sun for a few days, which matters here in SW Florida since freshly exfoliated skin is more sun-sensitive. Pause retinoids and exfoliating acids for about seventy-two hours, skip saunas and heavy sweat briefly, keep skin hydrated, and do not pick or scrub. If pairing with facial waxing, allow a gap, commonly about a week.

An important boundary: all injectable PRF here is Diana's RN-led lane, distinct from Amber's topical PRF, which is applied over microchanneling and never injected. description: Permanent jewelry is a clasp-free bracelet, anklet, necklace, or ring that Aundrea custom-fits to your body and micro-welds closed in seconds, so there is no clasp to catch, lose, or fumble. Metal choices are sterling silver, 14k gold-filled, and 14k solid gold, each with its own look, durability, and care. The piece is ready to wear immediately, so you can shower, sleep, and swim in it. Aundrea begins with a thorough double cleanse to lift makeup, oil, and SPF, then reads your skin to choose the right products for the day. From there the session moves through a gentle exfoliation to loosen dull surface buildup, a round of light steam and any comfortable extractions your skin calls for, and a finishing layer of serum, moisturizer, and SPF. It is designed to leave skin looking clean, smooth, and lit-from-within, and because everything stays at the surface there is no meaningful downtime — many clients book it on a lunch break or before an evening out. It feels calming and unhurried even in a compact window, closing with a short massage as products settle. Honest limits: a 30-minute express facial is maintenance and glow, not correction. It supports the appearance of brighter, fresher skin, but it will not resurface deeper texture, fade established pigment, or address laxity — those goals point to a longer treatment or an advanced-lane option. Individual outcomes vary, and your provider confirms what suits your skin that day.
who_its_for: Ideal for anyone who wants a fast, reliable glow — a busy schedule, a same-day event, or a first professional facial to see how your skin responds. It is also a comfortable entry point for sensitive or reactive skin because it stays gentle and surface-level. If you are looking to work on deeper texture, congestion, or a specific concern over time, a longer facial (the Luxe or Royal Rose) or an advanced-lane treatment is the better fit.
process: Quick skin read and double cleanse to remove makeup, oil, and SPF | Gentle exfoliation to loosen dull surface buildup | Light steam with any comfortable, appropriate extractions | Targeted serum and hydrating massage as products settle | Moisturizer and broad-spectrum SPF to finish

faqs:
Q: Is 30 minutes really enough time for a facial?
A: Yes — the Signature Rose is built as a focused express glow. It streamlines cleanse, exfoliate, and finish into a compact, effective refresh. If you want extractions, massage, and masking with more time to relax, the hour-long Luxe Rose Facial is the step up.

Q: Will I have any downtime or redness?
A: There is no meaningful downtime. Skin may look slightly flushed for a short while after extractions, which usually settles within a couple of hours, and you can return to your day right away.

Q: Can I wear makeup afterward?
A: Yes — many clients do the Signature Rose before an event and apply makeup the same day once the skin has settled. Give freshly exfoliated skin a little time and finish with SPF first.

Q: How often should I book it?
A: Because it follows the skin's roughly monthly renewal rhythm, a session about every four weeks keeps the glow consistent. Your provider will personalize the cadence to your skin and goals.

title: Skin Reset Facial
tagline: A deeper reset for stressed skin.
description: The Skin Reset Facial is Brandy's deep-clean treatment — 50 minutes focused on skin that feels congested, clogged, or in need of a proper clear-out. Where a classic facial keeps things balanced, this one leans into decongesting: the goal is to clear the look of buildup, blackheads, and clogged-looking pores and leave skin feeling genuinely reset. Brandy opens with a double cleanse and a careful skin read, then applies a clarifying exfoliation to soften the surface and warm steam to open things up, followed by thorough, comfortable extractions — the heart of this treatment. A purifying or balancing mask calms and refines the skin afterward, and a lightweight hydrating finish with SPF restores comfort without heaviness. It is designed to support the appearance of clearer, smoother, more even skin and to feel like a fresh start for skin that has been looking dull or clogged. The experience is still relaxing, but the emphasis is on the clean. Downtime is minimal; skin can look flushed after focused extractions and typically settles within a few hours. Honest limits: this is a maintenance-tier deep-clean facial for the appearance of congestion, not a medical acne treatment and not a corrective treatment for scarring — persistent or inflammatory acne is better served by a dedicated program, and your provider will guide you. Not every client is a candidate; individual outcomes vary.
who_its_for: Best for clients whose skin feels congested, oily, or clogged and who want a thorough professional clear-out. It is a strong choice when blackheads and clogged-looking pores are the main frustration. If your skin is dry, sensitive, or simply due for maintenance, the gentler Signature Facial or Lunch Time Glow may suit you better; for persistent or inflammatory acne, your provider may point you toward a dedicated acne program.
process: Double cleanse and careful skin read | Clarifying exfoliation to soften surface buildup | Warm steam to prepare the skin | Thorough, comfortable extractions to decongest | Purifying or balancing mask to calm and refine | Lightweight hydration and broad-spectrum SPF to finish
competitor_pricing: Local facial market: Ästhetik (PG) signature facial $160; Spago and Skin Sanctuary facials ~$90–$200. HoR $140 is near the Ästhetik signature.
faqs:
Q: Is this an acne treatment?
A: It is a deep-clean maintenance facial that supports the appearance of clearer, decongested skin — not a medical acne treatment. If you are dealing with persistent or inflammatory acne, your provider can point you toward a dedicated program that is better suited to it.

Q: Will the extractions hurt?
A: Extractions can feel like brief pressure, especially in congested areas, but Brandy works carefully to keep it comfortable. Skin may look a little flushed right after, which settles within a few hours.

Q: How much downtime is there?
A: Minimal — because this facial includes focused extractions, skin can look flushed for a few hours afterward before settling. You can return to your day, ideally with SPF and a light finish.

Q: How often should I get it?
A: For congested skin, some clients start with a session every few weeks and then ease into monthly maintenance as things clear. Your provider will tailor the plan to your skin.

Q: How is it different from the Signature Facial?
A: The Signature Facial is balanced, all-around maintenance. The Skin Reset puts the emphasis on a deeper clean and thorough extractions for skin that feels clogged or congested.

title: Soft Glam / Event Makeup
tagline: Elevated glam for your event.
description: Soft Glam / Event Makeup is a 45-minute application for a polished, camera-ready look with a little more drama — the sweet spot between everyday and full glam. It is built for prom, engagement and family photos, date nights, birthdays, and any occasion where you want to look elevated but still like yourself. Aundrea works in professional Jane Iredale mineral makeup, chosen for longevity and a finish that photographs cleanly without the harsh white flashback some conventional formulas throw under a flash. She preps and primes the skin, builds a longer-wearing base with color correction and concealing, then layers a soft-glam eye — typically a blended shadow, defined lashes, and subtle depth — with sculpted cheeks, defined brows, and a coordinated lip. The look is built to hold up through an event and read beautifully in photos. There is no downtime, and the mineral finish stays comfortable through a long day or evening. For weddings and important photography, a separate trial run beforehand is strongly recommended so colors, foundation match, and the exact look are locked in before the day — framed as coordination, never pressure. Honest limits: makeup is cosmetic; it enhances and evens the appearance of the skin and does not treat any skin condition, and post-treatment timing always defers to your provider. For a bride or a maximum, long-haul glam look, the Full Glam / Bridal application is the tier above; for a quick natural refresh, Everyday Makeup is the lighter option.
who_its_for: Perfect for prom, photos, date nights, and celebrations where you want a defined, photo-ready look that still feels like you. The skin-first mineral approach suits anyone who wants clean, comfortable, long-wearing coverage. If you are the bride or want the fullest, longest-wearing glam, choose Full Glam / Bridal; if you want a quick, understated everyday look, Everyday Makeup is the lighter, faster option.
